items.title: Support x402 payments on Solana end to end
items.body:
Verdikt can only verify a payment made on an EVM chain. Several services already
registered on the marketplace price in Solana, so this is a gap in what the
marketplace can actually serve, not a hypothetical.

`flights.verdikt.eth` is the clearest case: its 402 offers exactly one option, on
`solana:5eykt4UsFv8P8NJdTREpY1vzqKqZKvdp`, paid in SPL USDC with a sponsor
`feePayer`. There is no EVM option to fall back to, so the service cannot be paid
through Verdikt at all — a live listing nobody can buy from. `portfolio` and
`pnl` both advertise Solana alongside their EVM options, so an agent that prefers
Solana is pushed onto the EVM leg for no reason other than our limitation.

## What makes this more than adding a chain

A Solana payment identifies its payer as an ed25519 public key. Every part of
Verdikt downstream of the payment assumes that identity is an EVM address: the
bond, the verdict and the refund all live on Arc, refunds are credited to a payer
and claimed by that payer. A Solana-paying agent has nothing to claim with.

So the payment leg and the refund leg have to be answered together. Paying on
Solana while being unable to collect a refund would be worse than not supporting
it — the SLA promise is what the marketplace sells, and it would silently not
apply to those calls.

This depends on #61 (claiming a refund by signature rather than by sender) and
overlaps #59 (letting an agent name its own refund address). Both were opened for
the EVM case, where the same assumption already misfires: the Gateway and vanilla
schemes credit two different identities for the same wallet, and refunds are
currently sitting split across both. Solana is that assumption breaking
completely rather than partially, so whatever settles #61 should be checked
against it.

## Worth establishing early

- Whether CRE can observe Solana at all from the confidential workflow, and
  under simulation as well as production. The runtime clearly knows Solana as a
  chain family, but our verification path has only ever read EVM chains.
- Whether a verdict written for a Solana-paid call is meaningful to the rest of
  the system — the aggregate, the dashboard and the verdict history are all keyed
  on the assumption that a payer is an address.

## Done when

An agent can pay a Solana-priced service through the proxy, the call is verified
and a verdict written, and a failed call leaves that agent able to actually
collect its refund.

items.title: feat: migrate x402-proxy-template to x402 v2 with Solana support
items.body:
## Summary

Upgrades `x402-proxy-template` from x402 v1 to the current v2 protocol (`@x402/*` 2.19.0) and adds Solana support alongside Base. The legacy `x402-*` v1 packages haven't shipped since April 2026, and the template was hard-coded to a single EVM network.

Out of the box the template now advertises **Base Sepolia and Solana devnet** payment options on every protected route. `NETWORK` takes CAIP-2 identifiers (single or comma-separated) — the v1-era friendly names are gone entirely; a config still using one gets an explicit error naming the CAIP-2 format to switch to.

## What changed

- Middleware: legacy `x402-hono` → `@x402/hono` with EVM + Solana schemes registered per configured network.
- New `PAY_TO_SOLANA` var for Solana recipients (defaults to the well-known incinerator, mirroring the existing `0x…dEaD` testing default).
- Test client (`test-client.ts`) rewritten on `@x402/fetch` — works with an EVM key, a Solana key, or both.
- Playwright spec and all docs (README/AGENTS/TESTING/wrangler comments) updated to the v2 wire format.
- Removed the unused `@coinbase/x402` dependency and the legacy `x402` dev dependency.

## Verification

Settled real USDC end-to-end (402 → pay → verify → settle → JWT cookie → cookie-only re-access) on all four networks, each confirmed on-chain:

- Base Sepolia via `x402.org/facilitator`: [`0xcceef5…d46b95e`](https://sepolia.basescan.org/tx/0xcceef5f00d539fb8b303419718c499026aa37a38ac0daad96c7eab264d46b95e)
- Solana devnet via `x402.org/facilitator`: [`DsvS3mgZ…pQdTtDw`](https://explorer.solana.com/tx/DsvS3mgZ1wN4EfYuzF8cKy1D3Eg2oN1YAdKXXRUKHtF4Lz2ErLt5LdCUmsFDXQrTMqBsPmd1CmKv47fQpQdTtDw?cluster=devnet)
- Base mainnet via `facilitator.payai.network`: [`0x5676db…49fe35e`](https://basescan.org/tx/0x5676db1d0ea9f95fea89dff0c807a0571da8e8ecb1b9268fdf70ca08d49fe35e)
- Solana mainnet via `facilitator.payai.network`: [`3M8mbwoc…owr5kTa`](https://solscan.io/tx/3M8mbwocVoUo4gc54w6siDj3wbHP5hLkUZ5KYU7yqbBhRwidkXDzCv9a3BAQWcpLU65qE5Ky5QTSC6jMqowr5kTa)
- Out-of-the-box defaults, zero config changes: settled devnet USDC to the incinerator — [`258nvX9v…1NRqiPp`](https://explorer.solana.com/tx/258nvX9v7i737SuhxfsxyqPEF8P9s5Burtubf4sFd5CwCPVxfsKzdLHTjMwYVHEbcEtYuPU1RFBgNHH3T1NRqiPp?cluster=devnet)

Checks: `npm run lint` clean, Playwright 5/5, `pnpm run check` green.

## Notes for AI Agent Reviewers

<details>
<summary>Implementation and verification detail</summary>

### Implementation

- **Middleware construction** (`src/auth.ts`): an `x402ResourceServer` registers `ExactEvmScheme` for `eip155:*` and `ExactSvmScheme` for `solana:*` networks, wrapped by `@x402/hono`'s `paymentMiddleware`. The middleware is memoized at module scope keyed by a fingerprint of (facilitator URL, networks, recipients, route config), so the facilitator `/supported` sync runs once per isolate instead of per request. Measured: first protected request ~620 ms (sync), subsequent ~8 ms.
- **Route matching**: the template's `/*`-suffix patterns are converted to x402 v2 route patterns whose compiled regexes are a strict superset of the template's `startsWith` semantics; `index.ts` remains the outer gate, and both matchers are first-match-in-insertion-order, so pricing selection is consistent.
- **Network resolution**: CAIP-2 identifiers only (`eip155:*`, `solana:*`). Non-CAIP-2 entries (including pre-v2 names like `base-sepolia`) and missing per-family recipients return a JSON 500 config error with guidance (matching the existing `JWT_SECRET` error pattern) rather than crashing.
- **Recipients**: `PAY_TO` covers `eip155:*`; `PAY_TO_SOLANA` covers `solana:*` and defaults to `1nc1nerator11111111111111111111111111111111`, whose devnet USDC token account already exists — necessary because the v2 `exact` SVM scheme (unlike v1) does not create the recipient's associated token account, so a fresh address fails verification with a simulation error until it has received the token once. This constraint is documented in the README and wrangler comments.
- **Runtime**: `nodejs_compat` compatibility flag added — the v2 middleware uses `Buffer` in its settlement path.
- **Test client**: `wrapFetchWithPayment` + `x402Client` with optional EVM (`PRIVATE_KEY`) and Solana (`SOLANA_PRIVATE_KEY`, `SOLANA_RPC_URL`) signers; the client pre-filters the server's `accepts` to registered schemes, so either key works alone. Added `TARGET_PATH` override (defaults to `/premium`; the built-in `/__x402/protected` works without configuring an origin), prints the decoded `PAYMENT-RESPONSE` settlement receipt (network + tx hash), surfaces decoded rejection reasons on failed payments, and consumes response bodies so the process exits cleanly.
- **E2E spec**: v2 assertions — requirements in the base64 `PAYMENT-REQUIRED` header, `x402Version: 2`, both default accepts (including the incinerator payTo and facilitator-injected `extra.feePayer`), and the SDK's static HTML fallback for browser requests when `@x402/paywall` isn't installed.

### Compatibility

- The 402 challenge is now v2-only (header-carried requirements). Custom API clients written against the v1 body format need a v2 client such as `@x402/fetch` — `test-client.ts` shows the pattern.
- The default facilitator (`https://x402.org/facilitator`) verifies both shipped testnets, including the Solana devnet fee-payer sponsorship (`extra.feePayer`) the SVM scheme requires. Payers need no ETH/SOL: EVM payments are signed offline (EIP-3009) and Solana fees are sponsored via `extra.feePayer`; the facilitator submits transactions.

### Additional manual verification (`wrangler dev`)

- `GET /__x402/health` → 200; `GET /__x402/config` → resolved networks + masked per-family recipients.
- `GET /__x402/protected` (default config) → 402 whose decoded `PAYMENT-REQUIRED` carries both accepts — `eip155:84532` (USDC, amount `10000`) and `solana:EtWT…` (devnet USDC mint `4zMMC9…`, `extra.feePayer` injected).
- `NETWORK="base-sepolia"` → explicit 500 config error: `unknown NETWORK entry "base-sepolia"; use CAIP-2 identifiers such as eip155:84532`.
- Solana network enabled without `PAY_TO_SOLANA` → JSON 500 config error.
- Browser UA + `Accept: text/html` → 402 HTML fallback page.
- Each settlement above was independently confirmed on-chain (receipt status / transaction meta + recipient balance deltas).

</details>

Implements the first two tickets of the Solana rail from `docs/SOLANA-ARCHITECTURE.md` §9. The Solana peers (`@x402/svm`, `@solana/kit`) are optional and lazy — a Base agent never resolves them.

## SOL-01 — buyer `exact`
- `src/solana.ts`: `SOLANA_NETWORKS` (CAIP-2 + v1 names, mints, RPCs), `normalizeSolanaKey`, a `node:crypto` Ed25519 `solanaSigner`, `usdcBalanceMicroSolana` (plain JSON-RPC), `encodePaymentSolanaExact`.
- `src/live.ts`: `family()` / `isMainnet()` / `mainnetName()`; `createLiveAgent`, `selectOffer` and `sameChain` branch by rail. EVM path unchanged.
- `src/cli.ts`: `doctor` gains a `solana libs` probe and Solana wallet-key / rpc rows; `initLive` and `confirmMainnet` accept Solana networks.

## SOL-02 — `exact` seller via CDP
- `src/seller.ts`: `advertise()` returns an array; a Solana offer uses the USDC mint as `asset`, the canonical CAIP-2 network, and `extra.feePayer` from the facilitator's `/supported` (no EIP-712 `extra`). The gate skips the local flat amount/payee check for Solana (both live inside the signed transaction) and defers to the facilitator. The v1 Base 402 body stays byte-identical.
- `src/chain.ts`: optional `Facilitator.supported()` + `FacilitatorKind`.
- `src/facilitator-cdp.ts`: `CdpFacilitator.supported()` (`GET /platform/v2/x402/supported`). The CAIP-2 network reaches CDP verbatim, so the working EVM mainnet path is untouched.

## Real-money guard fix (from review)
`confirmMainnet`, `topup` and `limit` compared the bare string `"base"`, which the CAIP-2 alias (`eip155:8453`, `solana:5eykt…`) slipped past once `family()` began accepting CAIP-2. All three now route through `isMainnet()`, which resolves both spellings. Guarded by `test/network-mainnet.test.ts`.

## Notes
- `CdpFacilitator.supported()` / `/verify` for Solana follow the v2 spec shape but have not been round-tripped against live CDP (needs credentials) — flagged honestly in code comments, same posture as the existing v2 EVM path.
- Deps: `@x402/svm`, `@solana/kit`, and `@solana-program/token` declared; the last was a phantom (transitive) dep the wire test imported directly.

## Tests
`solana-wire`, `seller-solana`, `network-mainnet`, `no-solana-*` (proves a Base agent never loads the Solana peers), extended `facilitator-cdp`. **119 pass, `tsc --noEmit` clean.**

# Proposal: Add Base & Solana chain support to SDK

> **Status:** Proposed
> **SDK Target:** `ipfs-pay-to-pin-client@2.0.0` (current: `1.1.1`, Algorand-only)
> **Full doc:** `docs/proposals/multi-chain-expansion-base-solana.md`

---

## Problem

The current SDK only supports Algorand for x402 payments. This limits adoption because:

- EVM-native AI agents (Base is the most popular L2 for agentic workflows) can't use it
- Solana-native agents can't use it
- Most Web3 boilerplate templates target EVM chains first

Competing x402 facilitators (GoPlausible, Coinbase/CDP) already support Base and Solana.

## Current State

```typescript
// sdk/src/index.ts (current)
import { ExactAvmScheme, toClientAvmSigner, ALGORAND_MAINNET_CAIP2, ALGORAND_TESTNET_CAIP2 } from '@x402/avm';
import algosdk from 'algosdk';

// Network CAIP-2 is fixed at construction
this.networkCaip2 = network === 'mainnet' ? ALGORAND_MAINNET_CAIP2 : ALGORAND_TESTNET_CAIP2;
```

The SDK uses `@x402/avm` and `algosdk` exclusively — no abstraction layer for other chains.

## Proposal

### 1. Add Base (EVM) Support

Use the x402 protocol's EVM payment scheme. **Gas fees are covered by the GoPlausible facilitator** — they sponsor transaction fees across all supported chains. The SDK only needs to construct a valid EVM payment transaction and sign it.

### 2. Add Solana Support

Integrate with Kora RPC via the x402 Solana scheme. GoPlausible's facilitator integrates with Kora for gasless transaction signing. The flow:

1. Client creates Solana transaction with USDC payment instruction
2. Client sends to facilitator via `X-PAYMENT` header
3. Facilitator verifies via Kora's `signTransaction` (gasless)
4. Facilitator submits to Solana via `signAndSendTransaction`

### 3. SDK Architecture

```
IpfsPayToPinClient
├── ChainRouter (dispatches to correct x402 scheme)
│   ├── Algorand: ExactAvmScheme + algosdk
│   ├── Base: EvmScheme + ethers/viem + USDC (EIP-3009 / Permit2)
│   └── Solana: SolanaScheme + @solana/web3.js + Kora facilitator
├── PaymentAbstraction (unified pinFile, renewPin, getPinStatus)
└── GatewayClient (HTTP layer)
```

Public API stays the same — chain is transparent to the user.

## Gas Fee Summary

| Chain | Gas Token | Fee Sponsorship | Client Requirement |
|-------|-----------|-----------------|-------------------|
| Algorand | ALGO (microUSDC ASA) | Facilitator sponsors | Algorand wallet + mnemonic |
| Base | ETH (L2 gas) | **Facilitator sponsors** | Base wallet + mnemonic |
| Solana | SOL (compute units) | **Facilitator sponsors** | Solana wallet + mnemonic |

**The GoPlausible x402 Facilitator currently sponsors gas fees across all supported chains.** The client SDK does not need to manage gas directly — it only needs to construct the correct payment transaction and sign it.

## Implementation Priority

1. **P0:** Base (EVM) — highest adoption potential, Coinbase's public facilitator available at no cost
2. **P0:** Solana — growing agentic AI ecosystem, Kora RPC integration
3. **P1:** Unified chain abstraction layer — let SDK auto-discover from gateway
4. **P2:** Multi-chain token support — accept any USDC variant

## References

- [GoPlausible x402 Facilitator](https://algorand.co/blog/introducing-the-goplausible-x402-facilitator-payments-and-intelligence-for-agentic-commerce-on-algorand) — "Gasless and free... currently sponsoring transaction fees"
- [x402 Facilitator Docs](https://docs.x402.org/core-concepts/facilitator) — multi-chain payment flow
- [Kora x402 on Solana](https://solana.com/docs/payments/agentic-payments/x402-facilitator) — gasless signing via Kora RPC
- [Coinbase x402 on Solana](https://eco.com/support/en/articles/12328618-x402-protocol-explained-how-ai-agents-pay-onchain) — "Public facilitators from Coinbase (via CDP) available for Base, Solana at no cost"

# NEXUS-GEMINI x402: Autonomous Agentic Commerce & Strategic Intelligence Platform
## Complete Master Engineering & Architectural Thesis

---

### Executive Summary

Modern enterprise artificial intelligence has achieved unprecedented reasoning, planning, and natural language synthesis capabilities with foundation models such as Google Gemini 3.7. However, artificial intelligence agents remain severely bottlenecked by an archaic operational paradigm: **the Digital & Economic Friction Wall**. 

Whenever an autonomous software agent requires real-time, high-fidelity external intelligence—ranging from localized ASEAN supply-chain freight costs and cold-chain compliance data to live foot-traffic footfall counts—it is blocked by traditional Web2 paywalls. In current commercial architectures, utilizing an external paid API requires a human operator to register an account, configure institutional credit cards, manage monthly recurring SaaS subscriptions, generate static API access tokens, and store sensitive secrets. Furthermore, traditional payment rails (such as credit cards or wire transfers) impose minimum transaction thresholds ($0.30+ fixed per-transaction fee on Stripe/Visa/Mastercard), rendering sub-cent or fractional-dollar **data micropayments mathematically and economically unfeasible**.

**NEXUS-GEMINI x402** resolves this fundamental paradigm limitation by establishing an end-to-end, multi-agent autonomous commerce and intelligence architecture. By pairing **Google Gemini 3.7 Flash reasoning** with the **RFC-standard HTTP 402 Payment Required handshake protocol** and **Solana's sub-second, sub-cent SPL Token micropayment rail**, NEXUS-GEMINI transforms AI from a passive text chatbot into an active, economically-governed, self-sovereign agentic fleet capable of autonomous discovery, economic evaluation, cryptographic micropayment execution, and verifiable on-chain strategic synthesis.

---

## 1. What Inspired the Project

The inspiration for NEXUS-GEMINI x402 stems from two convergent tectonic shifts in technology:
1. **The Rise of Autonomous Agentic Reasoning**: With the advent of Gemini 3.7's hybrid thinking and structured tool orchestration capabilities, AI systems are no longer simply answering questions—they are decomposing high-level human objectives into multi-step execution graphs.
2. **The Emergence of Machine-to-Machine (M2M) Micro-Economies**: As businesses in high-growth corridors (specifically Southeast Asian SMEs in Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, and Thailand) attempt cross-border market expansions, the data they need is distributed across fragmented, localized data providers.

Human decision-makers and AI copilots are currently paralyzed by account-creation friction. If an AI agent evaluating a manufacturing plant in Johor needs 5 seconds of container throughput data from Port of Tanjung Pelepas, it shouldn't need a $5,000/month enterprise subscription. It needs to pay **$0.15 USDC directly to the data oracle in 400 milliseconds**, acquire the verified payload, verify the block proof, and immediately incorporate that insight into the strategic expansion model.

NEXUS-GEMINI x402 was built to prove that autonomous economic agency is not science fiction—it is viable today when grounded in strict human budget governance, mathematical hurdle rates, and sub-second cryptographic settlement.

---

## 2. Mathematical Formulations & Economic Governance Models

To prevent uncontrolled budget leakage, prompt injection vulnerabilities, or runaway execution loops, NEXUS-GEMINI x402 operates under strict mathematical bounds.

### 2.1 The Agentic Business Value (ABV) Equation
The platform quantifies the aggregate business value delivered by an autonomous multi-agent execution run via the multiplicative **ABV Index**:

$$\text{ABV} = I \times E \times C \times T$$

Where:
- **$I \in [0, 10]$ (Intelligence Quality)**: Evaluates the Gemini Commander's reasoning depth, semantic decomposition fidelity, and multi-source synthesis coherence.
- **$E \in [0, 10]$ (Execution Success)**: Measures the ratio of successfully discovered, negotiated, and completed HTTP 402 data handshakes without retry exhaustion.
- **$C \in [0, 10]$ (Economic Efficiency)**: Evaluates the Expected Value ($\text{EV}$) unlocked per unit of USDC spent from the agent treasury:
  $$C = \min\left(10, \frac{\sum \text{EV}_{\text{unlocked}}}{\sum \text{Cost}_{\text{settled}}} \times \alpha\right)$$
- **$T \in [0, 10]$ (Trust & Governance Compliance)**: Measures absolute adherence to human budget constraints ($B_{\max}$), verifiable zero-leakage cryptographic proof, and absence of hallucinated facts.

$$\text{Scale Range: } 0 \le \text{ABV} \le 10{,}000$$

### 2.2 The Strategic Intelligence Value (SIV) Index
To assess cross-functional strategic balance across intelligence domains, the SIV metric calculates the geometric product of six normalized domain parameters:

$$\text{SIV} = \left( R \times A \times C \times E \times G \times L \right) \times 100$$

Where:
- **$R \in [0.0, 1.0]$ (Research Relevance)**: Query alignment with target SME objective.
- **$A \in [0.0, 1.0]$ (Analysis Rigor)**: Statistical confidence and econometric modeling.
- **$C \in [0.0, 1.0]$ (Multi-Agent Coordination)**: Inter-agent latency and handover fidelity.
- **$E \in [0.0, 1.0]$ (Execution Completion)**: Successful acquisition of all targeted oracles.
- **$G \in [0.0, 1.0]$ (Governance Compliance)**: Zero deviation from human boundary parameters.
- **$L \in [0.0, 1.0]$ (System Learning & Cache Hit Rate)**: Reusability of acquired verified data.

### 2.3 The Economic Purchase Hurdle Rate ($\text{EV} > \text{Cost}$)
Before the **Commerce Agent (`NEXUS-04-SOL`)** is permitted to sign any Solana transaction, the **Strategy Agent (`NEXUS-03-STR`)** must verify the economic green light condition:

$$\mathbb{E}[\text{Value}] > \kappa \cdot \text{Cost}_{\text{USDC}} \quad \text{subject to} \quad \sum_{i=1}^{k} \text{Cost}_i \le B_{\max}$$

Where:
- $\kappa \ge 1.5$ is the risk-adjusted hurdle multiplier.
- $B_{\max}$ is the immutable human-authorized mission ceiling.

---

## 3. The Five-Agent Specialized Fleet Architecture

```
                                  [ Human Intent / Natural Language Goal ]
                                                    │
                                                    ▼
                                  ┌───────────────────────────────────┐
                                  │   01. Gemini Commander Agent      │
                                  │       (NEXUS-01-CMD)              │
                                  │  - Semantic Goal Decomposition   │
                                  │  - Bounds B_max Budget Ceiling   │

                                  │  - Scans ASEAN x402 Data Oracles  │
                                  │  - Benchmarks Latency & Quality   │
                                  └─────────────────┬─────────────────┘
                                                    │
                                                    ▼
                                  ┌───────────────────────────────────┐
                                  │   03. Strategy Agent              │
                                  │       (NEXUS-03-STR)              │
                                  │  - Computes EV > Cost Hurdle Rate │
                                  │  - Grants Economic Purchase Auth  │
                                  └─────────────────┬─────────────────┘
                                                    │
                                                    ▼
                                  ┌───────────────────────────────────┐
                                  │   04. Commerce Agent (x402)       │
                                  │       (NEXUS-04-SOL)              │
                                  │  - Intercepts HTTP 402 Challenge  │
                                  │  - Signs Sub-Second Solana Devnet │
                                  │  - Unlocks Payload with Proof     │
                                  └─────────────────┬─────────────────┘
                                                    │
                                                    ▼
                                  ┌───────────────────────────────────┐
                                  │   05. Verification Agent          │
                                  │       (NEXUS-05-VRF)              │
                                  │  - Validates Slot & Block Finality│
                                  │  - Produces Cryptographic Receipt │
                                  └─────────────────┬─────────────────┘
                                                    │
                                                    ▼
                                  ┌───────────────────────────────────┐
                                  │   Final Strategic Synthesis       │
                                  │   (Executive Brief + ROI Model)   │
                                  └───────────────────────────────────┘
```

1. **`NEXUS-01-CMD` (Gemini Commander)**: Uses Gemini 3.7 Flash to decompose high-level business goals into specific required external data variables. It enforces human budget constraints ($B_{\max}$) and establishes the analytical framework.
2. **`NEXUS-02-DSC` (Discovery Agent)**: Probes distributed HTTP 402 endpoints across Southeast Asia, querying metadata headers (`X-402-Price`, `X-402-Recipient`, `X-402-Network`, and quality scores) to construct candidate purchase vectors.
3. **`NEXUS-03-STR` (Strategy Agent)**: Evaluates ROI, expected value vs micro-cost ratios, and cross-checks with historical cache to avoid redundant expenditure.
4. **`NEXUS-04-SOL` (Commerce Agent)**: Executes the programmatic HTTP 402 handshake:
   - Initial `GET /api/x402/query` $\rightarrow$ Intercepts `402 Payment Required`
   - Encapsulates Solana keypair in devnet sandboxed vault
   - Submits SPL USDC transfer instruction
   - Awaits sub-second slot confirmation
   - Retries request with `X-Payment-Signature: <base58_signature>` $\rightarrow$ Receives `200 OK`
5. **`NEXUS-05-VRF` (Verification Agent)**: Validates cryptographic signature uniqueness, recipient address matching, and generates immutable forensic audit proofs.

---

## 4. How the Platform Works: Step-by-Step Execution Sequence

1. **User Objective Formulation**: A business executive or analyst inputs a natural language mission (e.g., *"Evaluate Johor Bahru vs Penang for semiconductor logistics expansion under $2.00 USDC"*).
2. **Commander Initialization**: The Commander defines variables: Freight Index, Port Throughput, Cross-Border FX, and Labour Cost.
3. **Autonomous Discovery**: The Discovery Agent identifies two relevant data endpoints (`oracle-penang-freight` at $0.15 USDC and `oracle-cross-border-fx` at $0.05 USDC).
4. **Hurdle Verification**: Strategy Agent calculates total cost ($0.20 USDC) versus expected strategic decision value ($4.80 USDC) = 24.0x ROI ratio, well above the $\kappa = 1.5$ threshold.
5. **Micropayment Handshake**: The Commerce Agent pays the oracles via Solana Devnet with ~0.000005 SOL fee and 420ms finality.
6. **Data Injection & Synthesis**: Unlocked raw datasets are fed back into Gemini 3.7 Flash.
7. **Deliverable Production**: The UI immediately renders an interactive, multi-dimensional Strategic Report, featuring Executive Synthesis, Market Opportunities, Financial Feasibility Model, Risk Assessment & Mitigation Matrix, 3-Phase Action Plan, and on-chain Solscan receipts.

---

## 5. Technical Stack

| Layer | Technologies Used | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| **Foundation LLM** | Google Gemini 3.7 Flash (`@google/genai`) | High-speed structured reasoning, intent decomposition, and econometric synthesis |
| **Blockchain Settlement** | Solana Devnet & SPL Token Standard | Sub-second micro-settlement, non-custodial agent vaults, immutable audit ledger |
| **Protocol Specification**| RFC HTTP 402 Payment Required Handshake | Universal web standard for programmatic machine-to-machine value exchange |
| **Backend Runtime** | Node.js, Express, TypeScript, `esbuild` | Server-side secure routing, API proxying, and key encapsulation |
| **Frontend UI** | React 18, Vite, Tailwind CSS v4 | High-Density tactical terminal layout, responsive telemetry pipelines, canvas-confetti |
| **Icons & Viz** | Lucide React, SVG Micro-charts | Visual telemetry, pulsing status indicators, and cryptographic receipts |

---

## 6. Challenges Faced & Solutions

1. **Challenge: Preventing Agent Spending Runaway**
   - *Solution*: Implemented a strict two-tier governance architecture: a hard-coded $B_{\max}$ lifetime cap in the server-side treasury vault and an auto-approve transaction threshold ($2.00 USDC).
2. **Challenge: Achieving True HTTP 402 Compliance**
   - *Solution*: Developed a RFC-compliant Express middleware that returns genuine `HTTP 402` status codes with `WWW-Authenticate: x402-solana-v1` and custom headers, verifying base58 Solana transaction signatures before unblocking data.
3. **Challenge: Eliminating Context Window Bloat**
   - *Solution*: Utilized specialized agent handoffs where intermediate agents only pass structured schemas and economic authorizations rather than raw LLM conversational history.

---

## 7. What We Learned

- **Micro-economies unlock real intelligence**: When AI agents can spend fractional cents on-demand, data providers are incentivized to expose high-value proprietary feeds without subscription lock-in.
- **Solana is the ideal settlement layer for agentic commerce**: Sub-second block times (400ms) match LLM reasoning speeds, and $0.00025 transaction costs make $0.05 micro-queries viable.
- **Human-in-the-loop governance builds enterprise trust**: Transparent visual telemetry, budget ceiling bounds, and on-chain cryptographic receipts provide the forensic auditability required for enterprise adoption.

---

## 8. Future Scalability & Commercial Roadmap

1. **Multi-Chain x402 Gateways**: Expanding from Solana to cross-chain liquidity pools via Wormhole and Circle CCTP.
2. **Decentralized Agent-to-Agent (A2A) Bidding Marketplaces**: Enabling autonomous AI agents to contract and pay sub-agents for specialized micro-tasks (e.g. Monte Carlo simulations, geospatial analysis).
3. **Cross-Border DuitNow / QRIS On-Ramps**: Direct fiat-to-Solana micropayment bridging for Malaysian and ASEAN SMEs.
4. **Enterprise Multi-Sig Vaults**: Integration with Squads Protocol on Solana for corporate multi-stakeholder governance over agent fleets.

items.title: Blocked on upstream: @x402/svm must move to @solana-program ^0.16/^0.18 before the kit 8 bump is cheap
items.body:
#358 bumps `@solana/kit` 5.5.1 → 8.2.0. It is safe to sign with and it costs 26% of the bundle. The cost is not intrinsic to kit 8 — it is caused by one upstream lag, and it disappears on its own when that lag clears. This issue records the unblock condition so the work is not repeated.

## Why it costs anything

`@x402/svm@2.21.0` (and `2.25.0`, current) still declares:

```json
"@solana-program/token": "^0.9.0",
"@solana-program/token-2022": "^0.6.1",
"@solana-program/compute-budget": "^0.11.0"
```

Those three peer on `@solana/kit: "^5.0"`, so bumping kit alone leaves three unmet peers directly on the payment-signing path. #358 forces them forward with `overrides` to `0.16.1` / `0.16.1` / `0.18.1`, which peer on `^8.0.0`. That override-driven nesting is what duplicates the stateless `@solana/*` packages — 20 copies of `@solana/errors`, 9 of `codecs-core` — and pushes `dist/cli.js` from **8.00 MB to 10.11 MB**.

`@solana/kit@8.2.0` installed on its own resolves to exactly one `@solana/errors`. kit 5.5.1 with `@x402/svm` and the *old* `@solana-program` versions also resolves to one. The duplication exists only in the overlap.

**Unblock condition: `@x402/svm` publishes a release whose own `@solana-program/*` deps are on `^0.16` / `^0.18`.** At that point #358 becomes a one-line version bump, the `overrides` come back out, and there is no bundle cost. `@x402/svm`'s own kit peer is already `>=5.1.0`, not `^5.0`, so it needs no waiver.

## Two mitigations already tried and failed — do not retry

1. `overrides` pinning all 20 `@solana/*` subpackages to 8.2.0 → bundle unchanged at 10.11 MB.
2. An esbuild `onResolve` plugin canonicalising `^@solana/` through `createRequire` → **worse**, 11.36 MB / 21 copies of errors.

## What is already settled, so nobody re-derives it

- Signing is byte-identical. Driving `@x402/svm`'s real `ExactSvmScheme.createPaymentPayload` and `ExactSvmSchemeV1.createPaymentPayload` with a fixed keypair, fixed blockhash and fixed memo against a stubbed RPC produces identical signed wire transactions under 5.5.1 and 8.2.0.
- All 32 symbols `@x402/svm` and ClawRouter import from kit / `@solana-program/*` exist in 8.2.0. Zero removed, zero renamed.
- The 2026-03-06 failure mode does not recur: one copy each of `@solana/signers`, `@solana/transactions`, `@solana/transaction-messages`. #375 now enforces that as a build guard, so a future bump cannot regress it silently.
- The duplicated packages are stateless — `@solana/errors` identifies by `e.name === "SolanaError"`, never `instanceof`.
- Peers are clean under the overrides: `npm ls` reports zero invalid, zero unmet non-optional.

## What the bump buys, honestly

Nothing demonstrable on this repo today. The `content-length` defect in `@solana/rpc-transport-http@5.5.1` is real — `body.length` is UTF-16 code units, not bytes — but it under-states only for **non-ASCII**, and every Solana RPC body on this path is ASCII (base58 addresses, base64 transactions, ASCII method names), where `String.length` equals the byte length and undici accepts the header. #352's own description called it "sensitive to … if", a hardening claim rather than a reproduced failure; the Solana `fetch failed` that *was* reproduced was an unreachable RPC endpoint, fixed separately in v0.12.271.

So there is no urgency, which is what makes waiting the right call rather than a deferral.

## When it does land

One real paid Solana call through the **built** bundle before release. The byte-identical result proves construction and signing agree between kit versions; it does not prove the facilitator accepts the transaction, and no test in the repo signs an SVM payment — `src/x402-sdk.test.ts` only asserts `registerExactSvmScheme` doesn't throw.

Also re-lock and rebuild `dist/`, which is committed here; #358 as it stands does not.

items.title: venice_x402_top_up_info drops live x402 v2 payment requirements
items.body:
### Summary

`venice_x402_top_up_info` exists to show step-1 top-up requirements (network, USDC asset, receiver, minimum amount). The live Venice `POST /v1/x402/top-up` discovery response is an x402 v2 `402` with `{ x402Version, accepts: [...] }`. `format402` in `src/format.ts` only understands two older shapes (`currentBalanceUsd` and `authOptions`), so the tool returns a successful-looking message that says the payment response is unrecognized and omits every `accepts` entry. Agents cannot complete a wallet top-up from this tool. The same formatter also hides those details when any other tool surfaces a 402 that uses the current protocol body.

### Problem

- Live discovery (auth-free) returns `402` with `x402Version: 2` and an `accepts` array of Base (`eip155:8453`) and Solana USDC options. Confirmed against `https://api.venice.ai/api/v1/x402/top-up` on 2026-08-24 (OpenAPI `20260824.012517`).
- `venice_x402_top_up_info` (`src/tools/index.ts`) POSTs `{ walletAddress, amountUsd }` and treats status `402` as success via `formatToolError`.
- `format402` (`src/format.ts`) never reads `accepts`, `payTo`, `asset`, `network`, or `amount`. Unknown 402 bodies become: `Payment is required, but Venice returned an unrecognized payment response.`
- The request body fields are not in the live schema (`properties: {}`; empty POST). `amount_usd` is ignored; the minimum is the `accepts[].amount` value (`5000000` = $5 USDC).
- Related but separate from #35 (Solana address regex + `SIGN-IN-WITH-X` header rename). Open PR #43 updates formatter wording only; it does not parse `accepts`.

### How to reproduce

1. On current `main`, run the tool (no Venice key required for discovery):

```js
// equivalent: POST https://api.venice.ai/api/v1/x402/top-up with {}
```

Or from a built server, call `venice_x402_top_up_info` with any `0x` + 40 hex wallet.

2. Observed (tool text, `isError` unset):

```text
⚠️ Venice returned 402 Payment Required.

Payment is required, but Venice returned an unrecognized payment response.
```

3. Expected: list each `accepts` entry (network, asset, payTo, amount in USD or base units, timeout). The live body includes those fields.

4. Local proof that the formatter is the drop: `formatToolError(new VeniceUpstreamError({ status: 402, body: <live 402 JSON> }))` produces the same unrecognized text and does not mention `eip155:8453`, `payTo`, or the $5 minimum.

### Fix proposal

- In `format402` (`src/format.ts`), add a branch for `x402Version` + `accepts[]`. Print network, asset, receiver (`payTo`), amount (USDC 6 decimals), and timeout. Keep the existing `currentBalanceUsd` / `authOptions` branches for inference 402s that still use those shapes.
- In `venice_x402_top_up_info` (`src/tools/index.ts`), POST an empty JSON object (or no body). Do not advertise `amount_usd` as a discovery input unless the API grows a real field.
- Add a unit test in `test/format.test.ts` using the live `accepts` fixture; add a tool test that a 402 with `accepts` is returned as readable text, not the unrecognized fallback.
- Caveat: do not echo arbitrary unknown 402 keys. Only format the documented x402 v2 fields. Header rename (`PAYMENT-SIGNATURE`) stays with #35.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `venice_x402_top_up_info` against live `POST /v1/x402/top-up` (or a mock of that 402 body) shows at least one Base and one Solana accept line with payTo, asset, and $5 minimum
- [ ] `formatToolError` on the live 402 fixture no longer contains `unrecognized payment response`
- [ ] Existing 402 fixtures in `test/format.test.ts` (`currentBalanceUsd`, `authOptions`, unknown body) still pass
- [ ] Non-goal: Solana address validation and `SIGN-IN-WITH-X` header migration (#35 / PR #43)
- [ ] Non-goal: implementing wallet signing or sending `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` from this server

items.title: @x402/svm: peerDependency allows @solana/kit >=5.1.0, but @solana-program/* pins hold it on kit 5
items.body:
### Summary

`@x402/svm` advertises support for `@solana/kit >= 5.1.0`, but its own dependencies pin `@solana-program/*` to versions that peer on `@solana/kit ^5.0`. A consumer on kit 6, 7, or 8 therefore gets an unsatisfiable peer graph and has to reach for `overrides` to install at all.

### Detail

`@x402/svm@2.25.0`:

```jsonc
"peerDependencies": {
  "@solana/kit": ">=5.1.0"          // advertises 6.x / 7.x / 8.x
},
"dependencies": {
  "@solana-program/token": "^0.9.0",
  "@solana-program/token-2022": "^0.6.1",
  "@solana-program/compute-budget": "^0.11.0"
}
```

Those pinned ranges resolve to the kit-5 line, and each declares:

| package | resolved | `@solana/kit` peer |
|---|---|---|
| `@solana-program/token` | `0.9.0` | `^5.0` |
| `@solana-program/token-2022` | `0.6.1` | `^5.0` (+ `@solana/sysvars ^5.0`) |
| `@solana-program/compute-budget` | `0.11.0` | `^5.0` |

Their current releases have moved to `^8.0.0`:

| package | latest | `@solana/kit` peer |
|---|---|---|
| `@solana-program/token` | `0.16.1` | `^8.0.0` |
| `@solana-program/token-2022` | `0.16.1` | `^8.0.0` |
| `@solana-program/compute-budget` | `0.18.1` | `^8.0.0` |

Because these are `^0.x` ranges, `^0.9.0` will never pick up `0.16.1` — so the pins are effectively frozen on kit 5 until they are bumped explicitly.

### Why this matters to us

We're on `@solana/kit@5.5.1` transitively through `@x402/svm`. `@solana/rpc-transport-http@5.5.1` sets

```js
"content-length": body.length.toString(),
```

where `body` is a string — a UTF-16 code-unit count, not a UTF-8 byte count. Upstream removed that header (present in `5.5.1`, `6.3.1`, `6.5.0`, `6.7.0`; gone from `6.10.0` on), so moving to kit 8 fixes it at the source. Today that upgrade is gated on this package rather than on anything in our own code.

### Bumping looks safe

items.title: fix(x402/v1): accept valid CAIP-2 chains missing from ChainIdToNetwork
items.body:
## Problem

Registering an x402 server on a chain that isn't in the hardcoded `ChainIdToNetwork` lookup (`apps/scan/src/lib/x402/chain-mapping.ts`) currently fails the whole resource with an opaque **"No valid x402 response found"**, even when the 402 challenge itself is fully spec-compliant (valid `scheme`, non-empty `accepts`, correct `payTo`/`asset`/`maxTimeoutSeconds`, etc).

Root cause: `networkSchemaV1` in `apps/scan/src/lib/x402/v1/schema.ts` `refine()`s that an `eip155:<id>` network string must have an entry in `ChainIdToNetwork`, or the whole field fails Zod validation:

```ts
z3.string().refine(
  v => v.startsWith('eip155:') && !!ChainIdToNetwork[Number(v.split(':')[1])],
  { message: 'Invalid network' }
)
```

Because this is inside `paymentRequirementsSchemaV1`, one unrecognized chain id in `accepts[]` fails the entire array parse via Zod — the integrator sees a generic parse failure with no indication that the actual issue is "your chain isn't in our static allowlist yet."

This is the same failure class already reported in #782 for a different chain (Stacks) — right now, no facilitator/network outside the ~17 hardcoded entries can register at all, regardless of spec compliance.

Concretely hit this running [TRIBUTE](https://gateway.tributex402.com) (x402 gateway on Robinhood Chain, `eip155:4663`, USDG settlement) through the registration flow — `/openapi.json` and `/.well-known/x402` both discover fine, all 6 paid routes return well-formed 402 challenges, but registration fails on every one with "No valid x402 response found."

## Fix

`normalizeChainId()` in `apps/scan/src/lib/x402/index.ts` already treats an unrecognized chain id as non-fatal:

```ts
result = ChainIdToNetwork[id] ?? chainId;
```

This PR brings the v1 schema validator in line with that same fallback instead of hard-rejecting: any well-formed `eip155:<numeric-id>` string is now accepted, and unknown chain ids fall back to the raw CAIP-2 string (exactly like `normalizeChainId` already does) instead of failing the parse.

```diff
- .refine(v => v.startsWith('eip155:') && !!ChainIdToNetwork[Number(v.split(':')[1])], { message: 'Invalid network' })
- .transform(v => ChainIdToNetwork[Number(v.split(':')[1])]),
+ .refine(v => v.startsWith('eip155:') && !Number.isNaN(Number(v.split(':')[1])), { message: 'Invalid network' })
+ .transform(v => ChainIdToNetwork[Number(v.split(':')[1])] ?? v),
```

Malformed input (`eip155:notanumber`, garbage strings) is still correctly rejected — only well-formed-but-unmapped CAIP-2 ids now pass through.

## What this does / doesn't do

- Does **not** touch `SUPPORTED_CHAINS`, CDP server wallets, onramp, or any Base/Solana-specific infra — those are a much bigger surface and out of scope here.
- Does **not** add Robinhood Chain (or any chain) to any "officially supported" list — it just stops the parser from hard-failing valid-but-unrecognized chain ids, so origins on any chain can at least register and display correctly instead of getting an opaque error.

## Testing

Added a regression test (`schema.test.ts`) covering the `eip155:4663` case, plus verified in isolation (outside the monorepo, since `pnpm@11.22.0` wasn't available in my sandbox) that:
- Known chains (`base`, `solana`) still resolve to their friendly names — no change.
- `eip155:4663` (previously failing) now parses and falls back to the raw CAIP-2 string.
- Garbage (`not-a-network`) and malformed (`eip155:notanumber`) input is still correctly rejected — no loosening of actual validation, just removal of the allowlist-only restriction.

```
=== BEFORE ===
eip155:8453 (Base, known)        -> base
eip155:4663 (Robinhood, unknown) -> FAIL: Invalid input
solana (named)                   -> solana
not-a-network (garbage)          -> correctly rejected
eip155:notanumber (malformed)    -> correctly rejected

=== AFTER ===
eip155:8453 (Base, known)        -> base
eip155:4663 (Robinhood, unknown) -> eip155:4663
solana (named)                   -> solana
not-a-network (garbage)          -> correctly rejected
eip155:notanumber (malformed)    -> correctly rejected
```

Happy to adjust scope/approach if maintainers have a preferred direction (e.g. surfacing the raw chain id differently in the UI, or a separate "unsupported chain" state vs silent passthrough).

items.title: deps: @solana/kit 5.5.1 → 8.2.0 (takes the content-length fix from upstream)
items.body:
Fixes the `content-length` defect #352 targets, by taking the fix upstream already shipped instead of patching it out of the bundle.

## The defect

`@solana/rpc-transport-http@5.5.1` (`dist/index.node.mjs:73,81`):

```js
const body = toJson ? toJson(payload) : JSON.stringify(payload);
...
"content-length": body.length.toString(),
```

`body` is a string, so `.length` is UTF-16 code units, not UTF-8 bytes. Measured against a local server: a 1-emoji body is 53 units / 55 bytes, and the request fails with `Unexpected end of JSON input`, then the connection desyncs. The library's own `DISALLOWED_HEADERS` and `FORBIDDEN_HEADERS` tables (lines 8, 17) list `content-length` as a header callers must not set — it then sets it anyway.

## Why upstream, not a build-time patch

Upstream deleted the line: present in `5.5.1`, `6.3.1`, `6.5.0`, `6.7.0`; gone from `6.10.0` on. `8.2.0`'s `createHttpTransport` is byte-identical to `5.5.1`'s minus that header. undici then computes `content-length` itself, correctly and in bytes — verified on Node 22.23.2 and 24.19.0, with no fallback to `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` (some RPC providers reject chunked).

**#352's build-time strip actively blocks this upgrade.** With kit 8 installed, its esbuild plugin hard-fails the build:

```
✘ [ERROR] strip-solana-rpc-content-length matched nothing in .../index.node.mjs
  — @solana/rpc-transport-http changed shape. Update the pattern; do not ship.
```

Its fail-closed condition is "a replacement occurred", so the build breaks precisely when the dependency becomes correct.

## Why this needs `overrides`

`@x402/svm@2.25.0` (latest) still pins `@solana-program/token ^0.9.0`, `token-2022 ^0.6.1`, `compute-budget ^0.11.0` — all peering on `@solana/kit ^5.0`. Their current releases (`0.16.1`, `0.16.1`, `0.18.1`) have moved to `^8.0.0`. So the clean bump is gated on the x402 SDK, not on this repo.

The overrides are **merged into** the existing block, not replacing it — the 13 entries already there are security pins (`ws`, `tar`, `postcss`, `basic-ftp`, `ip-address`, `brace-expansion`, `jayson/uuid`, …), all still enforced.

Forcing x402's transitive deps forward is safe because `@x402/svm` uses exactly four things from them — `findAssociatedTokenPda`, `getTransferCheckedInstruction`, `getSetComputeUnitLimitInstruction`, and the two program-address constants. Driven with identical inputs on both trees, every byte matches:

| | old (token 0.9.0 / cb 0.11.0) | new (token 0.16.1 / cb 0.18.1) |
|---|---|---|
| ATA (bump) | `FGETo8T8…ra8B` (254) | identical |
| transferChecked data | `0c87d612000000000006` | identical |
| transferChecked accounts | 4 accounts, roles `1,0,1,0` | identical |
| computeBudget data | `02400d0300` | identical |
| TOKEN / TOKEN_2022 program | unchanged | unchanged |

npm resolves **one deduped `@solana/kit@8.2.0`** — no second copy, which matters because `noExternal: [/.*/]` would bundle both.

## Verified

- `tsc --noEmit` clean
- 1088 passed / 1 skipped
- `npm run build` + dist smoke green
- built bundles carry **zero** manual `content-length` lines, with no patching of any kind

## NOT verified — needs a human before this ships

**A live Solana payment.** The only tests touching the signing path mock `@x402/svm` wholesale (`src/proxy.solana-rpc-override.test.ts:22,32`), and nothing in `src/` calls the token builders directly — they live inside x402's compiled code. Green tests say nothing about the real money path. One real Solana-rail paid request should gate the merge.

`dist/` is deliberately not regenerated here to keep the diff reviewable; `publish.yml` rebuilds from source anyway (`npm ci` → build → publish). Note main's committed `dist/` is separately stale.

items.title: feat(tx): adopt pay-kit's transaction path, Transaction V1 aware
items.body:
## Summary

Companion to solana-foundation/pay-kit#319 and solana-foundation/x402#11. Every place pay builds, signs, encodes, decodes or broadcasts a Solana transaction now goes through pay-kit's `core::tx`, `core::signing` and `core::rpc`. Legacy transactions are gone from pay: it builds version 0 everywhere, and version 1 (SIMD-0385) for operator-signed batches wherever the cluster gate is active. Stacked on `feat/x402-batch-settlement`; retarget to `main` once that lands.

## What changed

- **Dependencies**: pay-kit `1cfc850b`; solana-message ~4.4, solana-transaction ~4.1, solana-hash 4.4; surfpool main (the v1.4.0 tag predates V1); `[patch.crates-io]` on solana-keychain mirroring the kit workspace, to drop when keychain 2.0.0-beta.2 ships.
- **Ten sign-then-splice sites** (CLI gateway ATA creation, provider registration, subscription cancel direct and via gateway, pay-api redeem and subscription co-sign, operator plan broadcast, close-channels, bench fixtures and channel recovery) use the kit's slot signer and canonical (wincode) encoding. Blocking `RpcClient` sends go through `pay_kit::core::rpc`, since solana-rpc-client still serializes with bincode.
- **Push**: planner, permit and pay-api transfer batch work on `VersionedTransaction`, version 0 with the existing price-then-limit ComputeBudget prefix, so the wire is unchanged. The sponsor rejects legacy, lookup tables and any other version before validating the chunk. Both hand-mirrored chunk validators read the message through one static view.
- **Decoders** (transfer batch, subscription cancel, channel-open extraction, debugger correlation) accept versions 0 and 1 and reject legacy. `getTransaction` reads back with `maxSupportedTransactionVersion: 1`.
- **Servers** (Mpp, X402, upto, batch-settlement, session, subscription) are built with `with_tx_v1(Auto)`: one gate probe at startup, version 1 advertised and accepted when live. `settle-sessions`, `close-channels` and the session settlement worker pack at the probed version: 18 voucher settlements and 62 reclaims per transaction on V1 against 4 and 28.
- **Signers**: fee-payer signers are `Arc<dyn TransactionSigner>`. pay-api and pay-worker unwrap the keychain `Signer` enum into its Memory or GCP KMS backend, since the enum only signs messages.
- **Subscriptions**: adapted to pay-kit#316's wire rename (`planAddress`, `subscriptionProgram`, receipt `periodStart` / `periodIndex`; the receipt `reference` is the activation signature).

## Not in this PR

- `pay send --confidential` and pay-api's send endpoint delegate the confidential bundle to pay-kit; that bundle is on version 0 and still record-chunked. Collapsing it into one V1 transaction is the next kit change.
- Push chunks stay on version 0 (8 transfers). Moving them to V1 (~40 to 56 transfers) needs pay-api to advertise `transactionVersions` on the transfer-batch manifest.

## Verification

`cargo check --workspace --all-targets` and clippy clean; `cargo test --workspace` green, plus `cargo test -p pay-core --features server --test wrong_network_tests`.

- **`charge()` / `payFetch()`** — x402 in/out. `charge` is an Express middleware that charges per route; `payFetch` wraps `fetch` to auto-pay any 402 it hits. Both register `ExactEvmScheme` and `ExactSvmScheme`, so an agent can charge or pay on either chain.
- **`sweep`** — moves the agent's USDC balance to the owner's own wallet (`CASHFL0W_SWEEP_TO` / `CASHFL0W_SOLANA_SWEEP_TO` via `--chain solana`). `--swap` (EVM only) converts native balance to USDC through 0x first, carrying CASHFL0W's affiliate fee (`swapFeeBps`) — the monetization mechanic from the business plan. 0x doesn't route Solana, so there's no swap step there yet.
- **Facilitator** — defaults to no-signup options: `x402.org/facilitator` on EVM testnet, `pay.openfacilitator.io` on mainnet (free, no account, fee-free USDC settlement on Base and Solana). Swappable via `CASHFL0W_FACILITATOR_URL`; Coinbase's CDP facilitator documented as an opt-in alternative if KYT/compliance tooling is needed later.

## Test plan

# NEXUS-GEMINI x402: Autonomous Agentic Commerce & Strategic Intelligence Platform
## Complete Master Engineering & Architectural Thesis

---

### Executive Summary

Modern enterprise artificial intelligence has achieved unprecedented reasoning, planning, and natural language synthesis capabilities with foundation models such as Google Gemini 3.7. However, artificial intelligence agents remain severely bottlenecked by an archaic operational paradigm: **the Digital & Economic Friction Wall**. 

Whenever an autonomous software agent requires real-time, high-fidelity external intelligence—ranging from localized ASEAN supply-chain freight costs and cold-chain compliance data to live foot-traffic footfall counts—it is blocked by traditional Web2 paywalls. In current commercial architectures, utilizing an external paid API requires a human operator to register an account, configure institutional credit cards, manage monthly recurring SaaS subscriptions, generate static API access tokens, and store sensitive secrets. Furthermore, traditional payment rails (such as credit cards or wire transfers) impose minimum transaction thresholds ($0.30+ fixed per-transaction fee on Stripe/Visa/Mastercard), rendering sub-cent or fractional-dollar **data micropayments mathematically and economically unfeasible**.

**NEXUS-GEMINI x402** resolves this fundamental paradigm limitation by establishing an end-to-end, multi-agent autonomous commerce and intelligence architecture. By pairing **Google Gemini 3.7 Flash reasoning** with the **RFC-standard HTTP 402 Payment Required handshake protocol** and **Solana's sub-second, sub-cent SPL Token micropayment rail**, NEXUS-GEMINI transforms AI from a passive text chatbot into an active, economically-governed, self-sovereign agentic fleet capable of autonomous discovery, economic evaluation, cryptographic micropayment execution, and verifiable on-chain strategic synthesis.

---

## 1. What Inspired the Project

The inspiration for NEXUS-GEMINI x402 stems from two convergent tectonic shifts in technology:
1. **The Rise of Autonomous Agentic Reasoning**: With the advent of Gemini 3.7's hybrid thinking and structured tool orchestration capabilities, AI systems are no longer simply answering questions—they are decomposing high-level human objectives into multi-step execution graphs.
2. **The Emergence of Machine-to-Machine (M2M) Micro-Economies**: As businesses in high-growth corridors (specifically Southeast Asian SMEs in Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, and Thailand) attempt cross-border market expansions, the data they need is distributed across fragmented, localized data providers.

Human decision-makers and AI copilots are currently paralyzed by account-creation friction. If an AI agent evaluating a manufacturing plant in Johor needs 5 seconds of container throughput data from Port of Tanjung Pelepas, it shouldn't need a $5,000/month enterprise subscription. It needs to pay **$0.15 USDC directly to the data oracle in 400 milliseconds**, acquire the verified payload, verify the block proof, and immediately incorporate that insight into the strategic expansion model.

NEXUS-GEMINI x402 was built to prove that autonomous economic agency is not science fiction—it is viable today when grounded in strict human budget governance, mathematical hurdle rates, and sub-second cryptographic settlement.

---

## 2. Mathematical Formulations & Economic Governance Models

To prevent uncontrolled budget leakage, prompt injection vulnerabilities, or runaway execution loops, NEXUS-GEMINI x402 operates under strict mathematical bounds.

### 2.1 The Agentic Business Value (ABV) Equation
The platform quantifies the aggregate business value delivered by an autonomous multi-agent execution run via the multiplicative **ABV Index**:

$$\text{ABV} = I \times E \times C \times T$$

Where:
- **$I \in [0, 10]$ (Intelligence Quality)**: Evaluates the Gemini Commander's reasoning depth, semantic decomposition fidelity, and multi-source synthesis coherence.
- **$E \in [0, 10]$ (Execution Success)**: Measures the ratio of successfully discovered, negotiated, and completed HTTP 402 data handshakes without retry exhaustion.
- **$C \in [0, 10]$ (Economic Efficiency)**: Evaluates the Expected Value ($\text{EV}$) unlocked per unit of USDC spent from the agent treasury:
  $$C = \min\left(10, \frac{\sum \text{EV}_{\text{unlocked}}}{\sum \text{Cost}_{\text{settled}}} \times \alpha\right)$$
- **$T \in [0, 10]$ (Trust & Governance Compliance)**: Measures absolute adherence to human budget constraints ($B_{\max}$), verifiable zero-leakage cryptographic proof, and absence of hallucinated facts.

$$\text{Scale Range: } 0 \le \text{ABV} \le 10{,}000$$

### 2.2 The Strategic Intelligence Value (SIV) Index
To assess cross-functional strategic balance across intelligence domains, the SIV metric calculates the geometric product of six normalized domain parameters:

$$\text{SIV} = \left( R \times A \times C \times E \times G \times L \right) \times 100$$

Where:
- **$R \in [0.0, 1.0]$ (Research Relevance)**: Query alignment with target SME objective.
- **$A \in [0.0, 1.0]$ (Analysis Rigor)**: Statistical confidence and econometric modeling.
- **$C \in [0.0, 1.0]$ (Multi-Agent Coordination)**: Inter-agent latency and handover fidelity.
- **$E \in [0.0, 1.0]$ (Execution Completion)**: Successful acquisition of all targeted oracles.
- **$G \in [0.0, 1.0]$ (Governance Compliance)**: Zero deviation from human boundary parameters.
- **$L \in [0.0, 1.0]$ (System Learning & Cache Hit Rate)**: Reusability of acquired verified data.

### 2.3 The Economic Purchase Hurdle Rate ($\text{EV} > \text{Cost}$)
Before the **Commerce Agent (`NEXUS-04-SOL`)** is permitted to sign any Solana transaction, the **Strategy Agent (`NEXUS-03-STR`)** must verify the economic green light condition:

$$\mathbb{E}[\text{Value}] > \kappa \cdot \text{Cost}_{\text{USDC}} \quad \text{subject to} \quad \sum_{i=1}^{k} \text{Cost}_i \le B_{\max}$$

Where:
- $\kappa \ge 1.5$ is the risk-adjusted hurdle multiplier.
- $B_{\max}$ is the immutable human-authorized mission ceiling.

---

## 3. The Five-Agent Specialized Fleet Architecture

```
                                  [ Human Intent / Natural Language Goal ]
                                                    │
                                                    ▼
                                  ┌───────────────────────────────────┐
                                  │   01. Gemini Commander Agent      │
                                  │       (NEXUS-01-CMD)              │
                                  │  - Semantic Goal Decomposition   │
                                  │  - Bounds B_max Budget Ceiling   │
                                  └─────────────────┬─────────────────┘
                                                    │
                                                    ▼
                                  ┌───────────────────────────────────┐
                                  │   02. Discovery Agent             │
                                  │       (NEXUS-02-DSC)              │
                                  │  - Scans ASEAN x402 Data Oracles  │
                                  │  - Benchmarks Latency & Quality   │
                                  └─────────────────┬─────────────────┘
                                                    │
                                                    ▼
                                  ┌───────────────────────────────────┐
                                  │   03. Strategy Agent              │
                                  │       (NEXUS-03-STR)              │
                                  │  - Computes EV > Cost Hurdle Rate │
                                  │  - Grants Economic Purchase Auth  │
                                  └─────────────────┬─────────────────┘
                                                    │
                                                    ▼
                                  ┌───────────────────────────────────┐
                                  │   04. Commerce Agent (x402)       │
                                  │       (NEXUS-04-SOL)              │
                                  │  - Intercepts HTTP 402 Challenge  │
                                  │  - Signs Sub-Second Solana Devnet │
                                  │  - Unlocks Payload with Proof     │
                                  └─────────────────┬─────────────────┘
                                                    │
                                                    ▼
                                  ┌───────────────────────────────────┐
                                  │   05. Verification Agent          │
                                  │       (NEXUS-05-VRF)              │
                                  │  - Validates Slot & Block Finality│
                                  │  - Produces Cryptographic Receipt │
                                  └─────────────────┬─────────────────┘
                                                    │
                                                    ▼
                                  ┌───────────────────────────────────┐
                                  │   Final Strategic Synthesis       │
                                  │   (Executive Brief + ROI Model)   │
                                  └───────────────────────────────────┘
```

1. **`NEXUS-01-CMD` (Gemini Commander)**: Uses Gemini 3.7 Flash to decompose high-level business goals into specific required external data variables. It enforces human budget constraints ($B_{\max}$) and establishes the analytical framework.
2. **`NEXUS-02-DSC` (Discovery Agent)**: Probes distributed HTTP 402 endpoints across Southeast Asia, querying metadata headers (`X-402-Price`, `X-402-Recipient`, `X-402-Network`, and quality scores) to construct candidate purchase vectors.
3. **`NEXUS-03-STR` (Strategy Agent)**: Evaluates ROI, expected value vs micro-cost ratios, and cross-checks with historical cache to avoid redundant expenditure.
4. **`NEXUS-04-SOL` (Commerce Agent)**: Executes the programmatic HTTP 402 handshake:
   - Initial `GET /api/x402/query` $\rightarrow$ Intercepts `402 Payment Required`
   - Encapsulates Solana keypair in devnet sandboxed vault
   - Submits SPL USDC transfer instruction
   - Awaits sub-second slot confirmation
   - Retries request with `X-Payment-Signature: <base58_signature>` $\rightarrow$ Receives `200 OK`
5. **`NEXUS-05-VRF` (Verification Agent)**: Validates cryptographic signature uniqueness, recipient address matching, and generates immutable forensic audit proofs.

---

## 4. How the Platform Works: Step-by-Step Execution Sequence

1. **User Objective Formulation**: A business executive or analyst inputs a natural language mission (e.g., *"Evaluate Johor Bahru vs Penang for semiconductor logistics expansion under $2.00 USDC"*).
2. **Commander Initialization**: The Commander defines variables: Freight Index, Port Throughput, Cross-Border FX, and Labour Cost.
3. **Autonomous Discovery**: The Discovery Agent identifies two relevant data endpoints (`oracle-penang-freight` at $0.15 USDC and `oracle-cross-border-fx` at $0.05 USDC).
4. **Hurdle Verification**: Strategy Agent calculates total cost ($0.20 USDC) versus expected strategic decision value ($4.80 USDC) = 24.0x ROI ratio, well above the $\kappa = 1.5$ threshold.
5. **Micropayment Handshake**: The Commerce Agent pays the oracles via Solana Devnet with ~0.000005 SOL fee and 420ms finality.
6. **Data Injection & Synthesis**: Unlocked raw datasets are fed back into Gemini 3.7 Flash.
7. **Deliverable Production**: The UI immediately renders an interactive, multi-dimensional Strategic Report, featuring Executive Synthesis, Market Opportunities, Financial Feasibility Model, Risk Assessment & Mitigation Matrix, 3-Phase Action Plan, and on-chain Solscan receipts.

---

## 5. Technical Stack

| Layer | Technologies Used | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| **Foundation LLM** | Google Gemini 3.7 Flash (`@google/genai`) | High-speed structured reasoning, intent decomposition, and econometric synthesis |
| **Blockchain Settlement** | Solana Devnet & SPL Token Standard | Sub-second micro-settlement, non-custodial agent vaults, immutable audit ledger |
| **Protocol Specification**| RFC HTTP 402 Payment Required Handshake | Universal web standard for programmatic machine-to-machine value exchange |
| **Backend Runtime** | Node.js, Express, TypeScript, `esbuild` | Server-side secure routing, API proxying, and key encapsulation |
| **Frontend UI** | React 18, Vite, Tailwind CSS v4 | High-Density tactical terminal layout, responsive telemetry pipelines, canvas-confetti |
| **Icons & Viz** | Lucide React, SVG Micro-charts | Visual telemetry, pulsing status indicators, and cryptographic receipts |

---

## 6. Challenges Faced & Solutions

1. **Challenge: Preventing Agent Spending Runaway**
   - *Solution*: Implemented a strict two-tier governance architecture: a hard-coded $B_{\max}$ lifetime cap in the server-side treasury vault and an auto-approve transaction threshold ($2.00 USDC).
2. **Challenge: Achieving True HTTP 402 Compliance**
   - *Solution*: Developed a RFC-compliant Express middleware that returns genuine `HTTP 402` status codes with `WWW-Authenticate: x402-solana-v1` and custom headers, verifying base58 Solana transaction signatures before unblocking data.
3. **Challenge: Eliminating Context Window Bloat**
   - *Solution*: Utilized specialized agent handoffs where intermediate agents only pass structured schemas and economic authorizations rather than raw LLM conversational history.

---

## 7. What We Learned

- **Micro-economies unlock real intelligence**: When AI agents can spend fractional cents on-demand, data providers are incentivized to expose high-value proprietary feeds without subscription lock-in.
- **Solana is the ideal settlement layer for agentic commerce**: Sub-second block times (400ms) match LLM reasoning speeds, and $0.00025 transaction costs make $0.05 micro-queries viable.
- **Human-in-the-loop governance builds enterprise trust**: Transparent visual telemetry, budget ceiling bounds, and on-chain cryptographic receipts provide the forensic auditability required for enterprise adoption.

---

## 8. Future Scalability & Commercial Roadmap

1. **Multi-Chain x402 Gateways**: Expanding from Solana to cross-chain liquidity pools via Wormhole and Circle CCTP.
2. **Decentralized Agent-to-Agent (A2A) Bidding Marketplaces**: Enabling autonomous AI agents to contract and pay sub-agents for specialized micro-tasks (e.g. Monte Carlo simulations, geospatial analysis).
3. **Cross-Border DuitNow / QRIS On-Ramps**: Direct fiat-to-Solana micropayment bridging for Malaysian and ASEAN SMEs.
4. **Enterprise Multi-Sig Vaults**: Integration with Squads Protocol on Solana for corporate multi-stakeholder governance over agent fleets.

items.title: fix(x402): re-read confirmed channel accounts through replica visibility lag
items.body:
## Why

An RPC provider can serve transaction status and account state from different replicas, so the channel PDA a confirmed open just wrote can be missing from the very next read. The upto and batch settlement servers treated that one read as authoritative and failed the request, with the payer's deposit already escrowed on chain.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Client
  participant F as Facilitator
  participant A as RPC replica A
  participant B as RPC replica B
  C->>F: signed channel open
  F->>A: broadcast and confirm
  A-->>F: confirmed
  F->>B: read channel PDA
  B-->>F: account not found
  F-->>C: failure, deposit already escrowed
```

## What

Ports the linear backoff from [x402-foundation/x402#3367](https://github.com/x402-foundation/x402/pull/3367).

| SDK | Site |
|---|---|
| Rust | x402 upto open, batch settlement deposit |
| Go | x402 upto open |
| Python | x402 upto open |

TypeScript is not here: its x402 upto facilitator lives in the vendored `@x402/svm` tarball, built from the `solana-foundation/x402` fork. That fork is 16 commits behind upstream and #3367 is among them, so it needs a fork bump plus `just x402-vendor`, not a source edit.

Two optional config fields, `channelReadMaxAttempts` and `channelReadBackoffStepMs`, unset or non-positive meaning the default.

Rust x402 also swaps `get_account_data` for a lookup returning `Option`, so absence is distinguishable from an unreachable RPC without matching on error text.

## How

One read becomes up to six, waiting `step * attempt`: 200/400/600/800/1000ms, 3.0s of budget. Linear rather than exponential because replica lag is a small multiple of Solana's ~400ms slot time, so doubling spends the budget on single waits far longer than the lag being absorbed.

**Only a confirmed absence is re-read.** RPC errors, decode failures, wrong owners and every binding check are visible answers, and each still fails on the first read with the error it raised before.

MPP carries the same bug independently, against the same on-chain program. It is a separate protocol with its own readers and no shared code path, so it ships separately in #311.
